title: Dimension-free marginal inequalities for pure three-party states
abstract: The quantum marginal problem, concerned with the compatibility of local and global properties of a multipartite quantum system, is arguably one of the fundamental questions in quantum theory. In this article we introduce a novel family of inequalities bounding the allowed local spectra of a pure tripartite state. The number of inequalities in this family grows with the dimension of the system. Most importantly, the inequalities hold for arbitrary dimensions. For equal local dimension at most 4, they generate the complete set of eigenvalue inequalities.
summary: This paper tackles the quantum marginal problem for three-party pure quantum states by deriving a novel family of dimension-free inequalities that constrain the allowed local spectra. Using advanced algebraic techniques, the authors establish that these inequalities are complete for low dimensions (up to 4), providing a powerful theoretical tool for characterizing multipartite quantum correlations.
main_problem: The paper addresses the quantum marginal problem (QMP), which investigates the compatibility constraints between local spectral properties and the global state of a multipartite quantum system.
main_result: The authors introduce a novel family of dimension-free inequalities that bound the allowed local spectra of a pure three-party state, which are complete for local dimensions up to 4.
method: The methodology involves developing general algebraic and variational bounds using recursive structures (Siewert's recursion) and a 'seed' framework, building upon established theorems like Klyachko's maximal-eigenvalue theorem.
model_or_system: The focus is on pure tripartite quantum states ($\psi \in \mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B \otimes \mathcal{H}_C$), analyzing the constraints on the local spectra of the reduced density matrices ($ho_A, ho_B, ho_C$).
key_observables: Local spectra (eigenvalues) of the reduced density matrices for the three parties (A, B, and C).
important_parameters: The local dimension of the system (especially the constraint $d \le 4$ for completeness), and the mass $\lVert\psiVert^2$.
main_assumptions: The derived inequalities provide an outer approximation of the true marginal polytope; they are proven to be complete only for local dimensions up to 4.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the text references numerous equations (e.g., (17), (29), (35)) that define the derived inequalities.
paper_structure: The paper builds from known fixed-dimension results to general, dimension-free inequalities by employing a recursive structure and a general 'seed' framework, culminating in the stated theorems and corollaries.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental, general constraints on the local structure of quantum states, which is crucial for understanding entanglement measures and the limits of local measurements in quantum information theory.
